cases.rationale: The /login handler puts the request password into a concatenated SQLite authentication query. This is a separate input-to-query path from /users.
The /users id query parameter is concatenated into a SQLite query without parameter binding.
The /post msg parameter is returned as unescaped HTML response content by Python code; browser interpretation is the impact condition.
The /guestbook comment is stored and later interpolated without HTML escaping into a table cell by Python code.
The /diag domain parameter reaches subprocess.check_output with shell=True when the deliberately vulnerable server is launched at risk level 3.
The /extract object parameter is Base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads when the deliberately vulnerable server is launched at risk level 3.
The /docs path parameter is converted to an absolute path and opened without limiting it to the documents directory. The separate URL branch is not this case.
The /home session parameter chooses SESSIONID and /login retains that identifier after authentication instead of rotating it. Both Python operations are required for this case.
The /settings handler changes an authenticated user's email from a GET parameter without a request-intent/CSRF token check. A browser cross-origin request is the impact condition.
The /admin response constructs protected content before merely appending a client-side login redirect when the cookie is absent; the Python handler does not deny the response.
The /jump path parameter is inserted by Python into an emitted browser-navigation script with no destination validation.
The vulnerable-mode Python response omits X-Frame-Options and frame-ancestors restrictions around the /danger account-deletion action; secure mode adds both.

The lesson demonstrates replay of an already acquired bearer session token. Token theft and expiry policy are not independently specified by this Python route; do not score mere bearer-token lookup as a Python false negative.

The optional TLS flag defaults off but the server binds only to localhost by default; this README-level transport lesson needs a distinct network/deployment threat model and has no dedicated attack route. CWE is reviewer-assigned, not XML metadata.
